item.title: Transport Malta suspends licence of cab operator running over 100 vehicles
item.description: Transport Malta suspended the operating licence of My Planet Cab Ride Limited with immediate effect after inspections found several of the company's vehicles did not meet public service vehicle regulations and were not being used exclusively for the company's services. The operator runs more than 100 vehicles across platforms such as Bolt and Uber, and its vehicles may no longer offer cab services under that licence. The company may appeal to the Administrative Review Tribunal.

item.title: Labour Party President: budget measures on non-EU workers stirred anti-foreigner sentiment
item.description: Alex Sciberras said the government's budget measures targeting non-EU workers have unintentionally spread anti-foreigner sentiment, while acknowledging that infrastructure and overpopulation concerns must be addressed. Speaking on Campus103.7, he also criticised former prime minister Joseph Muscat's description of "foreigners serving the Maltese" and urged caution in the language used, saying many in the party were uncomfortable with the revelations of the Yorgen Fenech trial.

item.title: GWU condemns assault on staff at Sports Direct Qormi outlet
item.description: The General Workers' Union condemned the assault on employees on duty at the Sports Direct outlet in Qormi, calling for those responsible to be held accountable. Police said one person suffered light injuries and that both parties filed separate reports. The GWU said workers should be able to perform their duties without violence, intimidation or abuse, and called for stronger protection for staff in roles more exposed to confrontation.

item.title: 15 prisoners deported from Malta over the past two months, minister says
item.description: Home Affairs and Security Minister Glenn Bedingfield said 15 prisoners had been deported from Malta during October and November after serving their sentences. The individuals, who came from Europe, Asia, Africa and North America, were returned to their respective countries; four had reached the end of their sentences while the other 11 had already served their time. Bedingfield said the process would continue, adding that the country's security is an absolute priority.

item.title: International arrest warrant issued for former Steward Healthcare CEO Ralph de la Torre
item.description: Maltese authorities have issued an international arrest warrant for Ralph de la Torre, the former Steward Health Care chief who has not appeared in Malta to face charges arising from the magisterial inquiry into the hospitals concession. The Constitutional Court dismissed his attempt to suspend or stop the criminal proceedings before they had begun. Court hearings were told that correspondence was ongoing with the US embassy and that de la Torre's lawyer had held talks with the Attorney General's office about him coming to Malta voluntarily; he was charged in May 2024 and has been a no-show at four sittings since.

item.title: Government reiterates pledge to introduce five days of family violence leave
item.description: Equality and Civil Rights Minister Rosianne Cutajar said the government "remains committed" to introducing five days of family violence leave for victims of domestic violence, one of the Labour Party's electoral pledges, but gave no timeframe. Speaking at a conference on violence against women and the world of work, she said victims should not have to choose between their safety and their job, and that employment provides stability and economic independence during the process of rebuilding a life.

item.title: Birkirkara council insists civic centre has no room for police station
item.description: The Birkirkara local council has called an urgent meeting over the police station issue, following minister Glenn Bedingfield's claim that the council was lobbying for a new station in the civic centre. The council says the civic centre is fully utilised and cannot host a police station, and a statement was issued by mayor Desirei Grech and executive secretary Christine Jo Mansue. Malta Today reported the same position on the matter.

item.title: Ten new social housing apartments to be built in Paola
item.description: Two social housing projects in Paola will deliver ten new apartments through a combined investment of around €903,000, developed by Housing Projects Solutions Ltd. The Triq ix-Xewk project covers five one-bedroom apartments with excavation due to finish next week and completion expected by mid-July 2027; the Triq Imbroll project, already at third-floor level, is expected to finish by the end of January 2027. Housing Minister Owen Bonnici visited the works.

item.title: Malta could become Mediterranean hub for tourism safety
item.description: Malta could become a hub for cooperation on best practices in visitor safety following initiatives discussed at the 11th Mediterranean Tourism Forum, organised by the Mediterranean Tourism Foundation with around 1,500 participants and four action labs. One proposal being explored is MEDREADY, alongside the AI Hotel Blueprint. Tourism Minister Jo Etienne Abela said Malta is positioning itself as a leader in the region on tourism safety.

item.title: Food safety warning over undeclared mustard in organic soba noodles
item.description: The Food Safety Authority has warned consumers allergic to mustard to avoid a batch of organic soba noodles because it contains undeclared traces of mustard. The product is the Australian brand Hakubaku, best before date 1/06/2028, lot number 12.6B. The authority said the product must not be consumed by persons who are allergic or intolerant to mustard.

item.title: Bail denied for man accused of trafficking crack cocaine
item.description: A 28-year-old man from Żejtun was remanded in custody on Friday after pleading not guilty to seven charges tied to cocaine trafficking, conspiracy to traffic drugs and possession of weapons. The case was among the court business reported on the day, alongside separate proceedings in which a mother and son were remanded over an alleged organised crime network.

item.title: Police investigating altercation at Sports Direct outlet in Qormi
item.description: Video footage of an altercation between a customer and staff at the Sports Direct outlet in Qormi during Black Friday circulated on social media, showing a punch being thrown. Hudson Group, which operates the store, said it was aware of an incident involving a group of individuals and that police were called and are speaking to those concerned. Police confirmed they were called to the scene at around 2pm and a police report has been filed.

item.title: Capsized Malta-flagged diesel ship to be towed to Spanish port of Cartagena
item.description: The Malta-flagged diesel carrier Med Emre, carrying 7,000 tonnes of fuel, will be towed to the Spanish port of Cartagena, the transport ministry said. The vessel overturned early on Thursday off Ibiza, killing its chief engineer, according to its owner YMN Tankers. The fuel has been contained and the ship stabilised in open waters, and environmental groups have flagged risks to the area's flora, fauna and fisheries.

item.title: President visits Multigas as the Kirkop company marks a century
item.description: President Myriam Spiteri Debono visited Multigas at its Kirkop plant as the company marks 100 years of industrial gas manufacturing in Malta, tracing its origins to L. Farrugia Sons in Ħamrun in 1926. She was welcomed by chairman Louis Farrugia and CEO Noel Micallef, and a bronze sculpture by Christopher Chetcuti was commissioned for the centenary. The firm supplies medicinal oxygen to hospitals, clinics and home patients.

item.title: Stop works order after viral video of excavator operator working from a crane
item.description: The Building and Construction Authority and the Occupational Health and Safety Authority halted work at a Santa Venera construction site after a video showed an operator using a hydraulic breaker on a building while the mini-excavator was suspended in mid-air from a crane. The operator was not wearing a hard hat and the machine was not visibly harnessed. The project, under permit PA 08473/24, involves demolishing an existing property for 57 apartments and 16 garages.

item.title: KM Malta Airlines in talks with Chinese carriers over codeshare
item.description: KM Malta Airlines is discussing a codeshare agreement with several Chinese airlines to reach the Asian market, executive chairman David Curmi said at the 11th Mediterranean Tourism Forum. Curmi acknowledged that Chinese tourist numbers in Malta are "not big" but said the airline is talking to Chinese carriers serving European airports the national carrier already flies to, adding that Malta should look east as well as west to increase Asian connections.

item.title: 65-year-old man dies after being crushed between a van and a concrete mixer truck in Ħal Farruġ
item.description: A 65-year-old Italian national died on Saturday morning after being pinned between a concrete mixer truck and a van at an industrial site in Ħal Farruġ. Police were alerted at around 7.15am and the man was pronounced dead at the scene despite efforts by medical personnel. The van was driven by a 57-year-old man from Żebbuġ. Magistrate Philip Galea Farrugia opened an inquiry, with police and the Occupational Health and Safety Authority also investigating.

item.title: European Court of Justice refuses to rule on Malta's disputed Bill 55 gaming law
item.description: The Court of Justice of the European Union rejected a request from an Austrian court to rule on whether Malta's gaming law, known as Bill 55, breaches EU law. Malta had objected that the referral was a "fictitious dispute" between two Austrian parties. Bill 55, introduced in 2023, allows Maltese gaming companies to refuse to enforce sentences handed down against them in foreign jurisdictions. The dispute reached the ECJ after Spielerschutz Sigma, a company suing Austrian gamblers, was told its legal advisers could not rely on the law.

item.title: Libyan institute withdraws court appeal over planned Ta' Ġiorni mosque
item.description: The Libyan Higher Vocational Institute in Ta' Ġiorni has instructed its lawyers to withdraw the court appeal against the refusal of its 2024 planning application for a two-storey mosque with a minaret for students, staff and administrators. The Planning Authority rejected the application and the planning appeals tribunal upheld the refusal in late September, after which the institute filed a court appeal on 19 October.
